sourceType: Verified partial practice based on a marked May 2024 Assessment 3 review. Suspicious or unclear uploaded answers are excluded.
sourceLimitations: The public review reveals only part of the 25-question quiz. One visibly suspicious marked item ('float' as a PIN-protected payment concept) is deliberately excluded rather than treated as correct.

questions.text: Which organisation has historically published surveys that count websites and report web-server software usage?
questions.explanation:
Netcraft is known for its long-running web server and internet infrastructure surveys.

Student note: This is a named-industry-source question, so remember what Netcraft measures rather than only memorising the word.

questions.text: Project management is best described as:
options: Formal techniques for planning and controlling work undertaken to achieve a specific goal
Only monitoring a financial investment portfolio
Only helping employees accept a new system
Only conducting a review after a project ends
questions.correctAnswer: Formal techniques for planning and controlling work undertaken to achieve a specific goal
questions.explanation:
Project management coordinates planning, execution, monitoring and control so a defined objective can be achieved within constraints.

Student note: A post-project review and change management are useful activities, but neither alone defines project management.

questions.text: In the US banking context, a network widely used for electronic transfers such as direct account debits is the:
questions.explanation:
ACH is a US electronic funds-transfer network used for transactions such as direct deposits and account debits.

Student note: Do not generalise ACH as the name of every country's payment network; it is a specific US system.

questions.text: Testing used to compare the performance of hardware or software against a standard or alternative is:
questions.explanation:
Benchmarking measures performance using comparable workloads or tests so systems can be evaluated against each other or against a baseline.

Student note: A benchmark needs comparable conditions to be meaningful.

questions.text: A firewall or gateway that makes filtering decisions using application-level information is commonly called an:
questions.explanation:
Application gateways/proxy firewalls operate with awareness of application protocols rather than relying only on basic packet-header fields.

Student note: Packet filtering looks mainly at network/transport fields; an application gateway understands higher-level protocol behaviour.

questions.text: In an HTTP response, can the message body contain the HTML page requested by the client?
questions.explanation:
For a normal successful HTML response, the response body carries the representation/content returned to the client.

Student note: Headers describe the response; the body carries the content when a body is present.

questions.text: An unchanging web page retrieved from a stored file on the server is a:
questions.explanation:
A static page is served largely as stored, instead of being generated for each request from application logic or database data.

Student note: Static does not mean the browser cannot style or display it interactively; it describes how the server content is produced.

questions.text: If a user wants to prevent tracking specifically through browser cookies, disabling cookies prevents sites from storing and reading those cookies.
questions.explanation:
Disabling cookies blocks cookie-based storage/tracking, although websites may still use other tracking techniques.

Student note: This answer is only about cookies; disabling cookies does not make a browser untrackable by every method.

questions.text: Which TCP/IP application protocol is specifically designed for transferring files?
questions.explanation:
FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol and is designed for transferring files between systems. Modern secure alternatives are often preferred in real deployments.

Student note: Learn the purpose as well as the abbreviation.

questions.text: Privacy/security, portability, independence and convenience are recognised concerns when evaluating digital-cash systems.
questions.explanation:
Digital-cash designs involve trade-offs around security, privacy, ease of use, acceptance/portability and dependence on intermediaries or platforms.

Student note: Payment technology is evaluated on both technical security and practical usability.

questions.text: What is the fixed-size result produced by a cryptographic hash function commonly called?
questions.explanation:
A cryptographic hash function maps input data to a fixed-size hash value, often called a message digest.

Student note: A digest is not encryption: you do not decrypt a hash to recover the original message.
